results.sentence: I've recorded a plan to measure the left and right hippocampal volumes (in mm3) for every session of the NMOSD cohort with SynthSeg (robust), the analysis that works on clinical T1w scans of any contrast or resolution and reports its own quality scores as checks — FreeSurfer would give the same volumes but at about 7 hours a session and under the lab's licence, so I chose the cheaper one. The pre-flight shows synthseg@1 with 0 of 0 units ready, about 0 min, no GPU needed; it is not ready yet because no stack of the selection is picked, so the release of the input would hold no subject's images — nils pick run picks them. You start it with Run.

I planned samseg-lesions (lesion on) over every visit of ms-cohort-a, so the white-matter lesion volume at each session shows how lesion load changes over time; the pre-flight counts 0 of 0 units ready, about 0 min, and it is not ready yet because no stack of the selection is picked, so the release of the input would hold no subject's images — nils pick run picks them. You start it with Run.

I recorded samseg-lesions (lesions on) over the first session of each subject in ms-cohort-b — 12 subjects, 47 sessions in the cohort, first scan each — because white-matter lesion volume is read from the T1w and FLAIR together, which is what this analysis does; no pre-flight was taken because the ask for the cohorts left no handle to check the run over, so the engine will count the units and flag any session missing a FLAIR when you press Run.

I've recorded a run of synthseg (robust) over the latest session of each subject in ms-cohort-a — 38 subjects, 38 sessions — to measure the left and right thalamic volumes; I chose it over FreeSurfer because it is the cheaper fit for thalamic volumes on clinical T1w scans. No pre-flight was taken because the ask for the cohorts left no handle to check the run over, so the engine could not count the units or flag missing inputs; you start it with Run.

I planned MRIQC (mriqc@1) over your selection ms-baseline@1 to measure each T1w's image quality — SNR, CNR, CJV, EFC, FBER, smoothness and non-uniformity — with its checks flagging low SNR (below 8) and high CJV (above 0.8), which is the direct answer to which scans are poor. The pre-flight shows 0 of 0 units ready, about 0 min, no GPU needed, but it is not ready: no stack of the selection is picked, so the release of the input would hold no subject's images; nils pick run picks them. You start it with Run.

I recorded FreeSurfer recon-all (freesurfer-recon-all@1) over all 47 sessions of ms-cohort-b — the field's reference for cortical thickness, the way you do it by hand — but the pre-flight shows 0 of 0 units ready (about 0 min, CPU, no GPU): no stack of the selection is picked, so the release of the input would hold no subject's images; nils pick run picks them, and it also needs the lab's FreeSurfer licence. Press Run when the picks are in place.

I recorded a plan to skull-strip each subject's first T1w in ms-cohort-a with synthstrip and read the brain's volume from the mask (measure.synthstrip.brain_volume) — the cheap, purpose-built choice for a skull strip, where synthseg would give you the same volume plus every structure. I've recorded a run of samseg-lesions with the lesion step switched off, so it segments each session's T1w alone and reports the whole-brain structure volumes plus the intracranial volume — that way the sessions in ms-cohort-b without a FLAIR are not missing, and it runs over all 47 sessions of the cohort; no pre-flight was taken because the ask for the cohorts left no handle to check the run over, so you start it with Run.

synthseg (robust) will measure the total intracranial volume from each session's T1w in selection every-t1@2 — it works on any contrast or resolution and its own quality scores are the checks.
